Because consoles are underpowered PCs. They simply don't have the performance to provide 60FPS, much less 100FPS in anything decent-looking.

TVs are easy, you just get an incoming signal and pass it along. In games, the GPU needs to actually render the frames in real time. More frames means more work and it pretty much scales linearly. So twice the frames = twice the required processing power. You can't get that for 400€.

NTSC is 30/60 FPS because the US power grid uses alternating current at 60 Hz. PAL is 25/50 FPS because the European power grid is 50 Hz.

Very few NTSC TVs actually display more than 60 FPS. Claims like "240 Hz" rely on frame interpolation and cause the "soap opera effect" by displaying frames that are not in the source material. HDMI 2.0 and up allows for 4K at a maximum of 60 Hz, but also 1080P at 120Hz, but not all 4K TVs will actually display 1080P@120 Hz. To get a signal of 1080P@120Hz on HDMI, you pretty much need a PC with an HDMI 2.0+ output.

Within the last few weeks, Samsung released firmware for some current 4K TVs enabling AMD Freesync variable refresh rate, to match the recent update to allow the XBox One X to use Freesync on its AMD graphics chip. Realistically that will enable the XBox to improve image quality by synchronizing framerates below 60 Hz, because consoles still generally don't have the power to run demanding games faster than (or at) 60 FPS.
